title: Attention Fusion Optimizer: prefill pacing audit and v2->v3 compatibility seam
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: After integrating FlashAttention v3 kernels for select topologies we observed reproducible latency variance and a 3-7% P95 regression for long-context chat workloads during prefill bursts. This ticket scopes an audit and mitigation path that focuses on two correlated areas: 1) the fusion/tiling decisions introduced by the v3 kernels (we call this the Attention Fusion Optimizer), and 2) prefill->decode pacing transitions where kernel warmup and KV-cache handoff expose scheduler jitter.
goals: 1) Identify root causes of P95 regressions tied to v3 fusion heuristics and prefill scheduling. 2) Build a small, portable micro-benchmark harness that reproduces the regression in CI. 3) Implement conservative gating in the kernel selector that prevents oscillation and reduces startup jitter for long prefill sequences. 4) Add telemetry signals and a canary rollout plan for runtime-1.22.
success_criteria: - Micro-benchmark reproduces P95 delta >= 4% in CI for a representative long-context workload. - New kernel-selector gate reduces P95 regression to <=1% relative to v2 baseline under the same load. - Canary rollout shows no increase in 5xxs or latency spikes across 100k requests (dashboard link). - Documentation and test harness merged in GH PRs.
approach: 1) Profiling: capture CPU/GPU timelines, kernel execution time distributions, and KV-cache churn during prefill. 2) Signal identification: add flags to emission that mark v2/v3 kernel usage, tiling config, and warmup hits. 3) Experiments: run controlled ramp experiments across instance types (A100/RTX) to compare v2/v3 behavior with identical inputs. 4) Mitigation: implement a Prefill Pacing Shim (PPS) in the runtime that enforces a short staged prefill cadence for long prefixes and a conservative v3 gate that requires sustained favorable metrics before switching. 5) Rollout: canary -> cohort -> global with automatic rollback triggers based on telemetry.

risks:
- PPS may add tail latency for small-batch low-latency workloads if misconfigured.
- Overly conservative gate delays v3 benefit for some models.
- Microbench may not capture multi-tenant noise seen in production; need cluster-level validation.
notes: Rationale for PPS: observed that when prefill length > 1024 tokens and decoding starts immediately, the first decode kernel often picks a different tiling configuration than the steady-state decode kernels, causing workspace reallocation thrashing. A short staged prefill cadence (50-200ms pacing) allows kernel prober to observe warm metrics and prevents immediate oscillation.
